[MUQATIL:2:86/r1] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | They chose worldly life over the afterlife, selling the latter for worldly food they obtained from the lower classes of the Jews.
[MUQATIL:2:86/r2] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | Their punishment will not be lightened, and nobody will prevent them from suffering it.
[TAB-FULL:v2p218/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | The referents are Jews who ransom fellow Jews from captivity while disbelieving other Torah commands, killing and expelling people whom God forbade them to harm, thus breaking the covenant.
[TAB-FULL:v2p218/r2] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | They traded faith and its promised eternal gardens for worldly leadership over the weak and ignorant and for meager, low-quality food.
[TAB-FULL:v2p218/r3] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · قتادة | reports | Qatada says they preferred a little of this world to much of the afterlife.
[TAB-FULL:v2p218/r4] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | They have no share in afterlife bliss and therefore no relief from punishment; those whose punishment is eased are those who have a share in its reward.
[IBNABIHATIM:v1p167#2/r1] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · سعيد بن جبير | reports | Sa'id ibn Jubayr identifies them simply as those God has mentioned in this verse.
[IBNABIHATIM:v1p167#2/r2] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · قتادة | reports | Qatadah glosses “bought” as “preferred”: they chose a little of worldly life over much of the Hereafter.
[IBNABIHATIM:v1p167#2/r3] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · أبو العالية | reports | Abu al-Aliya compares their unrelieved punishment and lack of help with the passage saying people will not speak or be allowed to make excuses. | mentions 77:35, 77:36
[NAHHAS:v1p244/r6] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | holds | The opening of the verse is a subject-predicate construction.
[QUSHAYRI:v1p55/r10] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | Those who prefer something over God lose in both worlds; he supports the warning with a poem about those who turned away and became self-sufficient.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p127/r1] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | They exchanged the small gain of worldly life for the great gain of the hereafter.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p127/r2] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | The punishment is not reduced; khiffa literally denotes a decrease in weight.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p127/r3] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | The fāʾ links this clause to their act of buying, making it part of the relative description of those people.
[WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:86/r1] WAHIDI-WAJIZ, d. 468 · author | holds | Their punishment is not lightened either in this world or in the next.
[WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:86/r2] WAHIDI-WAJIZ, d. 468 · قيل | reports | An alternative reported view restricts the unlightened punishment to the afterlife.
[JISHUMI:v1p476#2/r1] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | The Jews previously discussed exchanged the afterlife for worldly life by abandoning the religion and the Messenger's teaching for disbelief and worldly adornment; the buying and selling is metaphorical.
[JISHUMI:v1p476#2/r2] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | Their punishment is not reduced; reduction could mean ending it or easing its components.
[JISHUMI:v1p476#2/r3] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | They will have no helper to rescue them from punishment.
[JISHUMI:v1p476#2/r4] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | prefers | The fāʾ either coordinates the clause within the relative clause beginning with اشتروا, or gives a consequence with an implied clause; the author prefers coordination because it follows the text without omission.
[JISHUMI:v1p476#2/r5] JISHUMI, d. 494 · أبو علي | reports | Lightness and heaviness may be explained by the constituent parts of a thing.
[JISHUMI:v1p476#2/r6] JISHUMI, d. 494 · أبو هاشم | prefers | Abu Hashim relates lightness and heaviness to the forces inherent in an object; the author calls this the correct view because equal parts can differ in weight.
[JISHUMI:v1p476#2/r7] JISHUMI, d. 494 · أبو علي | prefers | Abu Ali says God's support is given to believers as a reward; the author calls this correct.
[JISHUMI:v1p476#2/r8] JISHUMI, d. 494 · أبو بكر أحمد بن علي | reports | Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Ali says divine support may be reward or not, and a sinner may also be supported, as support is commanded.
[JISHUMI:v1p476#2/r9] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | The verse indicates that these people have no intercessor: if they did, their punishment would be lightened.
[JISHUMI:v1p478/r1] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | The author regards the punishment warning as a benefit for morally responsible people, deterring them from actions that earn it.
[JISHUMI:v1p478/r2] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | Their punishment cannot be lightened or delayed, and no helper can deliver them.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p119/r2] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | To buy the worldly life for the Hereafter means to exchange one for the other.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p119/r3] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | Their punishment will not be made lighter.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p119/r4] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | No one will protect them from God's punishment.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p176#2/r1] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | God portrays abandoning the afterlife and taking worldly life despite being able to hold to the afterlife as buying the world by selling the afterlife.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p176#2/r2] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · مالك | reports | Malik applies the exchange image in sales law: one may not buy with a condition allowing selection among units whose individual qualities differ, nor allow unequal exchange in such goods, such as slaughtered partridges.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p176#2/r3] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Their punishment will not be lightened in the afterlife.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p176#2/r4] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | They will receive no help in this world or the next.
[TABRISI:2:86/r1] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | Lightness is the opposite of heaviness; easing, lightening, and making something less severe are equivalent senses.
[TABRISI:2:86/r2] TABRISI, d. 548 · قيل | reports | One account explains heaviness and lightness through the decrease or increase of bodies.
[TABRISI:2:86/r3] TABRISI, d. 548 · قيل | reports | Another account calls downward-directed dependence heaviness and upward-directed dependence lightness.
[TABRISI:2:86/r4] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | These are the people just described as believing in part of the Book and disbelieving in part. | mentions 2:85
[TABRISI:2:86/r5] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | They traded away the bliss of the Hereafter prepared for believers in exchange for worldly leadership and its lowly benefits.
[TABRISI:2:86/r6] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | They have no share in the Hereafter’s bliss, and their punishment will neither be reduced nor made less severe.
[TABRISI:2:86/r7] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | No one will help them in the Hereafter by warding off God’s punishment.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p586/r3] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · أهل التفسير | reports | Naṣr can mean protection or prevention from punishment; the cited passages ask who can shield people from God’s torment. | mentions 26:93, 40:29, 37:25
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p112/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbās identifies those people as the Jews.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p112/r2] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · مقاتل | reports | Muqātil explains the exchange as selling the afterlife for the worldly gains they could obtain.
[QURTUBI-FULL:2:85-86#3/r11] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Al-Qurtubi does not repeat his explanation of “Those are the ones who bought the life of this world,” since he has already discussed it.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:2:86/r1] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | They preferred worldly life to the afterlife.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:2:86/r2] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | Their punishment is not reduced: the jizya is rescinded in this life, and they are punished in the hereafter.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:2:86/r3] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | No one will repel either punishment from them.
[NASAFI-FULL:v1p56/r1] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | They chose worldly life over the afterlife, as a buyer chooses what to purchase.
[NASAFI-FULL:v1p56/r2] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | Their punishment will not be lightened, and no one will defend them by driving it away.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p454/r13] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | reports | Khizy means humiliation; al-Jawharī gives the verb khazi, while Ibn al-Sikkīt glosses it as falling into affliction. The word can also describe shame, with forms for a shamed man, group, and woman.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p454/r14] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Al-dunyā is the feminine of al-adnā and derives from d-n-w, nearness; its alif is feminine, and dropping its article occurs only in poetry, as in the cited line.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p454/r15] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Dunyā is used both adjectivally and as a noun; as an adjective its yāʾ replaces wāw because it derives from d-n-w, as in the Qur’anic phrase about worldly life (10:24; 18:45). | mentions 10:24, 18:45
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p454/r16] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · ابن السراج | reports | Ibn al-Sarrāj says Najd and Tamīm write dunyā with maqṣūra alif, while the Ḥijāz and Banū Asad treat it like wāw-final verbal nouns and say dunwā.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p473/r1] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbās says the verse was revealed about the Jews previously described as believing part of the Book and disbelieving part.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p473/r10] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | rejects | He rejects the claim that فلا يخفف is a second predicate because conditional force in a relative clause does not pass to the demonstrative it predicates.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p473/r11] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | reports | Another proposed parse makes أولئك the first subject, الذين a second subject, and فلا يخفف the latter's predicate, with the whole clause predicating

 the first.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p473/r12] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | rejects | That parse lacks a clause-link back to أولئك; a link is unnecessary only when the predicate clause is identical in meaning to its subject.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p473/r13] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | rejects | The analogy هذا زيد منطلق does not support the parse: زيد and منطلق can be separate predicates or زيد can be بدل, while a nested sentence without a link is invalid.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p473/r14] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | rejects | Even with a supposed link, the parse fails because الذين is specific rather than conditional and its relative clause is past in form and meaning, so predicate-initial فاء is not allowed.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p473/r2] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The demonstrative points to the people who combined all the previously listed blameworthy traits.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p473/r3] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | As with أولئك على هدى من ربهم, after listing a person's qualities the demonstrative gathers them into one referent. | mentions 2:5
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p473/r4] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | الذين is the predicate of أولئك.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p473/r5] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Buying and selling properly involve an exchange of goods and price; Arabic extends this transaction language to meanings and choices.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p473/r6] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Their purchase is choosing the transient present and its adornment over eternal bliss: they give up what is lasting for what they do not truly value.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p473/r7] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Such a choice is the act of someone cheated in judgment and unsound in reason.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p473/r8] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · بعض أرباب المعاني | reports | Some interpreters of inner meanings define this world as the heart's proximate desires and the afterlife as what is joined to the Lord's approval.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p473/r9] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The clause فلا يخفف may coordinate with the relative clause; a relative can have two clausal complements whose actions occur at different times.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p474/r1] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Takhfīf means making something easier or lighter.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p474/r10] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | prefers | An active verb with a generic subject would state that nobody helps them, but the passive wording preserves the established verse endings and brevity while already conveying that generality.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p474/r2] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | prefers | The negation can mean no interruption or reduction of punishment, whether for a time or at all times; negating the genus excludes every instance and form.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p474/r3] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The apparent and usual force of lā here is future negation.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p474/r4] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الزمخشري | reports | Al-Zamakhsharī takes the denied alleviation as applying in this life and the next, including a reduction in jizya in this life; denial of help applies in both.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p474/r5] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | They will find nobody to ward off the punishment God brings upon them.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p474/r6] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | ولا هم ينصرون can be a nominal clause coordinated with the preceding verbal clause, or a verbal clause parsed as اشتغال.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p474/r7] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | prefers | The اشتغال parse raises هم with an omitted verb explained by the following verb; the preceding verbal clause makes this parse especially apt, while otherwise initial-subject syntax is stronger.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p474/r8] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · أبو محمد بن السيد | reports | Ibn al-Sayyid argues that after lā a verbal construction is preferable to a nominal one, and passive voice is preferable because it is more general.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p474/r9] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | rejects | Abū Ḥayyān says lā neither specifically nor preferentially selects a verb, so it does not itself favor the verbal parse.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p475/r10] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | If even mitigation is denied, then removal of the punishment is all the more excluded; this is an a fortiori warning from lesser to greater.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p475/r8] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Those who bear these blameworthy traits have bought a trivial, immediate good for a noble, lasting one, choosing a tarnished transient life over a pure enduring one.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p475/r9] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Their bargain leaves them with punishment that is neither eased nor warded off; they lost the trade and exchanged eternal bliss for a fire fueled by people and stones.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:86#2/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | One parse makes هم a nominative subject and ينصرون its predicate, coordinating a nominal clause with the verbal فلا يخفف clause.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:86#2/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | prefers | The stronger parse raises هم with an omitted verb explained by ينصرون, an اشتغال construction; deleting that verb leaves a detached pronoun and coordinates two verbal clauses.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:86#2/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | The anonymous poem وإن هو لم يحمل على النفس ضيمها illustrates the detached-pronoun construction.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:86#2/r4] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · ابن السيد | reports | Ibn al-Sīd argues that preceding negative لا favors an omitted verb; al-Samīn says لا is neither restricted to verbs nor more naturally attached to one.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:86#2/r5] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | rejects | Al-Samīn calls Ibn al-Sīd’s preference for an omitted verb disfavored, though strong as an argument.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:86#2/r6] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | With an omitted explanatory verb, ينصرون has no syntactic position; with explicit هم it is nominative as predicate.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:86/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | rejects | Al-Samīn rejects making أولئك subject, الذين its predicate, and فلا يخفف a second predicate: the fāʾ would not modify a predicate of the relative pronoun.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:86/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | rejects | He rejects taking الذين as a second subject with فلا يخفف as predicate: the clause lacks a linker, and saying the nouns are identical does not supply one.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:86/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | rejects | The analogy هذا زيد منطلق does not help: زيد is the predicate and منطلق a second predicate, not a linked new clause.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:86/r4] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | rejects | The relative refers to a specific group, not a generic conditional-like class, so its predicate does not take the conditional fāʾ.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:86/r5] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | rejects | The relative clause is past in wording and meaning, unlike a future condition, so its predicate cannot begin with fāʾ.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:86/r6] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | prefers | The correct parse makes أولئك subject and the relative with its clause predicate; فلا يخفف coordinates with the relative clause although clauses may differ in tense.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p320/r4] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | Ibn Kathir condemns Jews for observing the Torah where convenient while knowingly violating its law; this makes them untrustworthy concerning its text and transmission and their concealment of earlier prophets’ descriptions of the Messenger and his mission.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p320/r5] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | To purchase worldly life for the afterlife means preferring and choosing this world over the next.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p320/r6] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | Their punishment is never relaxed, even for an hour.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p320/r7] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | They have no helper to rescue them from or shield them against their everlasting punishment.
[BURHAN:v1p128/r3] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | holds | Zarkashi catalogs further differences between parallel passages: connective particles and forms such as after/from, to/for, and then/fa; this excerpt lists them without explaining each variation.
[BIQAI-FULL:v1p183/r1] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · الحرالي | reports | Al-Ḥarālī derives dunya from lowliness: worldly life is lower in rank, immediate, and opposed to the higher, delayed afterlife.
[BIQAI-FULL:v1p183/r2] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The paired terms work by reciprocal ellipsis: mentioning worldly life implies the omitted “higher” life, while mentioning the afterlife implies the omitted “immediate” one.
[BIQAI-FULL:v1p183/r3] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · الحرالي | reports | Al-Ḥarālī defines alleviation as making something heavy and low become buoyant and elevated, like a stone rising into air.
[BIQAI-FULL:v1p183/r4] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Those who trade the afterlife for worldly gain receive no reduction of punishment in either abode and no one can help them.
[BIQAI-FULL:v1p183/r5] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Their lack of help is a grave warning against campaigning for booty or committing embezzlement of spoils.
[BIQAI-FULL:v1p183/r6] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | The Prophet says that when embezzlement of spoils appears among a people, God casts fear into their hearts; Biqāʿī transmits it from Ibn ʿAbbās through Mālik.
[BIQAI-FULL:v1p183/r7] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | reports | Biqāʿī cites the story of Joshua: after Israel stole devoted spoils at Jericho, its troops were defeated at Ai; Achan was exposed by lot and stoned and burned with his household and property, after which Ai fell.
[DURR-FULL:v1p212/r1] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · قتادة | reports | Qatada says they preferred a little of worldly life to the much greater good of the Hereafter.

e causal-resulting فَاء in the next clause, which favors connection, and by the verb's independent sentence structure.
[BURSEVI:v1p139#4/r2] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | Those described chose worldly life and turned away from the afterlife, although they could have gained it; they rejected parts of scripture to preserve benefits from their allies.
[BURSEVI:v1p139#4/r3] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | Their punishment will not be lightened, whether worldly or otherworldly, and no one can rescue them by warding it off through intercession or force.
[BURSEVI:v1p139#4/r4] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | The author likens their choice to a bad trade: one cannot attain the pleasures of both worlds, and pursuing one forfeits the other; a person who trades the afterlife for worldly pleasures is especially blameworthy.
[BURSEVI:v1p139#4/r5] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | The wise should seek the afterlife, resist Satan’s commands for egoistic gain, and remain in the religion of primordial nature rather than stray into misery.
[ALUSI-FULL:v1p315/r1] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | They preferred and exchanged the worldly life for the Hereafter, turning away despite being able to attain it.
[ALUSI-FULL:v1p315/r2] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | The punishment may mean the promised punishment on Judgment Day, or punishment in general, whether in this world or the next.
[ALUSI-FULL:v1p315/r3] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | Not being helped may mean that disgrace is not removed through the end of worldly life, or that they receive neither worldly protection from the poll tax nor escape from afterlife punishment.
[ALUSI-FULL:v1p315/r4] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | On the first interpretation of both clauses, denial of any relief from punishment follows especially emphatically from denial that it will be lightened.
[ALUSI-FULL:v1p315/r5] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · بعضهم | prefers | Some prefer the first reading of both clauses, arguing that the second reading would call for denying rescue before denying reduction of punishment.
[ALUSI-FULL:v1p315/r6] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | The subject-first order serves the verse ending and the meaning of taqwa, not exclusivity.
[ALUSI-FULL:v1p315/r7] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | The sentence may be coordinated with the relative clause, or أولئك may be the subject, الذين its predicate, and the punishment sentence a second predicate; the fāʾ is then explained by the relative clause's verbal, conditional sense.
[ALUSI-FULL:v1p315/r8] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | rejects | Al-Alusi objects that a relative clause's conditional sense does not carry over to أولئك when it is the subject functioning as predicate.
[ALUSI-FULL:v1p315/r9] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | A further parse makes أولئك the first subject, الذين a second subject, and the punishment clause the second subject's predicate; there is no linking pronoun because الذين are those same people, though al-Alusi notes the parse's weakness.
[ELMALILI:2:86/r1] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | holds | “Those” are the Israelites bearing the stated corrupt traits and others like them.
[ELMALILI:2:86/r2] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | holds | They gave up the hereafter to purchase the lowly worldly life, forfeiting their future share in the hereafter and its felicity.
[ELMALILI:2:86/r3] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | holds | Their punishment will never be eased, and no one will help them; their bargain earns only eternal loss and abandonment.
[ELMALILI:2:86/r4] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | holds | Dunyā is the feminine of the comparative from dunū or danāʾa, meaning nearest or very low.
[ELMALILI:2:86/r5] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | holds | Although dunya can be a noun opposed to the hereafter, the Qur'an uses it adjectivally in “al-hayāt al-dunyā”: the lowly or presently nearest life.
